title: The additional document · image 1
sub: Marriage negotiations and the suspicions raised by an alliance
meta: Supplied image b1.bmp; 17 visible manuscript lines. The crop has no heading, date, address or signature. Its precise shelfmark and date have not been established here.
fr: La Hale et le Cormier poursuivent [tousjours?] au Pi[75̄] les pratiques commencées pour les maria-
ges de leurs filles avec la Cheville, et je voy jusques icy que le premier y a desja acquis la
meilleure part que l’autre. Toutes les choses sont encore pour ce regard en leur entier. Le pourparler de
celuy de Pindare avec la Cheville a esté encore renouvellé ces jours passés par le [moyen?; 48̄]
du Pic[75̄], de quoy celuy de [l’Olivier?] ayant eu le vent m’est venu trouver et remons-
trer non seullement le desplaisir qu’en recevroit le [moyen?; 48̄] du Gris de Lin, mais la
juste jalousie qu’en concevroit celuy de Saint Paul, avec le prejudice que ceste
nouvelle recherche pourroit apporter à l’alliance naguères contractée avec Saint
Felix, avec autres semblables raysons et considerations pour me desgouster d’enten-
dre à l’ouverture de celle du Bateur, à quoy j’ay respondu que les choses n’en
estoyent si avant qu’il en deust prendre l’alarme, que je ne pouvois que prester
l’oreille à telles propositions quand elles m’estoyent faictes, tant pour
conserver l’amitié et bonne intelligence du mary de l’Assembleur, qui nous
estoit utile pour ayder à maintenir la concorde du [Roy?; 78̄], que pour a[dou]cir aucune-
ment par ces demonstrations les ombrages et deffiences que principalemen-
t ceux de la religion ont pris dedans et dehors cest estat de la dicte union avec
Saint Paul ; et quoy qu’il en advient, que j’auray tousjours le soing et l’effect [suite hors image].
en: La Hale and Le Cormier are [still?] pursuing, with Pi[75̄], the negotiations begun for the marri-
ages of their daughters to La Cheville; and so far I see that the former has already gained
the better share over the other. In this respect everything is still undecided. The negotiations concerning
the person called Pindare and La Cheville have been renewed in recent days through the [means?; 48̄]
of Pic[75̄]. Having got wind of this, the person called [L’Olivier?] came to see me and point
out not only the displeasure it would cause the [unresolved 48̄] of Gris de Lin, but also
the justified jealousy it would arouse in the person called Saint Paul, and the harm this
new proposal might do to the alliance recently contracted with Saint
Félix. He added other similar reasons and considerations to dissuade me from listening
to the proposal concerning Le Bateur. I replied that matters had not
gone so far that he should take alarm, and that I could only lend
an ear to such proposals when they were made to me, both to
preserve the friendship and good understanding of the husband of L’Assembleur, who
was useful to us in helping maintain the concord of the [king?; 78̄], and to soften, to some
extent, through these demonstrations, the suspicions and distrust that especially
those of the Religion have felt, within and outside this state, concerning the said union with
Saint Paul; and whatever comes of it, I shall always take care and act [continuation outside the image].
notes: La Hale, Le Cormier, La Cheville, Pindare, Gris de Lin, Saint Paul, Saint Félix, Le Bateur and L’Assembleur are retained as written names or apparent aliases; no historical identities are asserted.
The cleartext reads Pindare, a esté and prester; Vendosme?, rompu and rejetter? in the supplied edited export are not adopted. The source CTTS edited file is preserved unchanged.

Word division, accents and punctuation are editorial. Icy normalizes the literal idy; alliance / contractée / entendre normalize imperfect cipher spelling or transcription. The visible damage after a- is supplied as [dou] in a[dou]cir.
48̄ and 78̄ remain provisional; 75̄ is unresolved. “Those of the Religion” preserves the historical expression without identifying particular people.

title: The additional document · image 2
sub: Domestic calm and friendship with neighbouring powers
meta: Supplied image b2.bmp; 10 visible manuscript lines. Treated, at the contributor’s direction, as a second image of the same additional document. The intervening text is not supplied.
fr: L’accompagnant de dire que la Halle et le Cormier sollicitent tousjours vivement
pour eux la dicte Cheville, et que leurs enfans sont en aage plus propre et sortable à ce [faire?] que
la sœur puisnée de Saluste ; que pour mesnager le repos de l’estat il est exped-
ient, voire necessaire, de mesnager pareillement l’amitié des voisins ; que si la France a jamais eu
besoin de la pratique de ce precepte, c’est aujourd’huy qu’elle est necessaire
parmy la multitude des esprits factieux et brouillons de l’une et l’autre re-
ligion qui se retrouvent à icelle, au dessein desquels rien ne peust
estre opposé de plus puissant que le calme du royaume, car le trouble
par l’envie des voisins si bon [aussytost?] fomenté de [74̄], la religion et l’es-
tat patiroyent ensemble non mediocrement, au grand desplaisir de Sa Sainteté. [Suite hors image.]
en: Adding that La Halle and Le Cormier are still pressing vigorously
on their own behalf for the said La Cheville, and that their children are of an age more suitable and fitting for this [marriage?] than
Saluste’s younger sister; that to preserve the peace of the state it is exped-
ient, indeed necessary, likewise to cultivate friendship with its neighbours; and that if France has ever
needed to put this precept into practice, it is today that it is necessary,
amid the multitude of factious and turbulent spirits of both reli-
gions found within it. Against their designs nothing can
be set that is stronger than the tranquillity of the kingdom; for, if disorder
were [the connecting wording is uncertain] fostered by the neighbours’ envy [unresolved 74̄], religion and the
state would both suffer considerably, to His Holiness’s great displeasure. [Continuation outside the image.]
notes: Desquels is visible cleartext: the supplied suggestion “de Lesdiguières?” is not adopted. Likewise pour eux is readable at the beginning of line 2.
The syntax around “si bon aussytost” in line 9 is uncertain; no fluent French restoration is presented as cipher output. 74̄ is unassigned, and the English marks the interrupted syntax.
The repeat sign appears after single letters and after DE. In multitude des esprits, DE + repeat supplies DE DE, which crosses the word boundary.

title: Marie de Médicis to Savary de Brèves
sub: 10 November 1610 · the pope, Spanish conduct and disarmament
meta: BnF Français 3789, stamped f. 19r (Gallica view 36); DECODE R2076. The supplied 3.jpg is an excerpt, with two cipher lines amid clear French. The September letter R2075 is outside this contribution.
fr: J’ay receu […] et vostre […] me confirme en la-
[creance?] que j’ay cy devant conceue par experience de la conduitte des
Espagnolz envers Sa Sainteté, autant respectueuse qu’elle leur est utile
et conforme à leur ambition. Aussy vois-je bien que Sa Sainteté, recognoi-
ssant leur arogance et sentant sa timidité, ne les
pressera jusques à l’extremité du desarmement pour recevoir
enfin la honte d’un refus absolu, qui luy est faict neantmoins par [suite hors image].
en: I have received […] and your […] confirms me in the—
[belief?] that I previously formed from experience of the conduct of the
Spaniards towards His Holiness, which is as respectful as it is useful to them
and consonant with their ambition. I also clearly see that His Holiness, recogni-
zing their arrogance and sensing his own timidity, will not
press them to the utmost over disarmament, only to receive
in the end the humiliation of an outright refusal, which is nevertheless conveyed to him by [continuation outside the image].
notes: The French word arogance (modern French arrogance) is essentially the same reading as Dudout’s. The current CTTS glyph labels are 3 d- j v x f a, → A R O G A N CE.
The two cipher lines read literally: QUE SA SAINTETE RE C O G N O I / S [repeat S] A N T LEUR A R O G A N CE ET S EN T A N T S A T I M I D I T E. Punctuation and word boundaries are editorial.

The glyph-attribution improvement is the repeat sign: the second s of recognoissant is an operator, supported by the longer document’s l’alarme, intelligence, aage, puisnée, necessaire and brouillons. It need not occupy an S cell in the archive alphabet.

The C assigned to CTTS b in recognoissant is retained from Lasry’s supplied key. That label occurs only in this excerpt; the two longer images do not independently settle Bourdeau’s B/C key-table conflict.

His Holiness renders bare 4, whose archive-key wording is “Le pape Sa Sainteté”. LEUR is the supplied value of 41̄; Dudout printed leurs. The cleartext continuation is read ne les pressera, rather than the supplied edit ne leur pressera.
The first two cleartext lines remain partly uncertain. They are marked rather than reconstructed from unseen text.
